ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: After shifting the parabola \(y=x^{2}-4x+1\) to the left so that its vertex falls on the y-axis, as shown in the figure, what is the area \(S\) of the shape formed by the two parabolas, the line \(y=-3\), and the x-axis (the shaded area in the figure)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} The parabola $y=x^{2}-4x+1=(x-2)^{2}-3$ has its vertex at $C(2,-3)$. Shifting it leftwards to have the vertex lie on the y-axis, we get the vertex $B(0,-3)$. Point $A$ is one of the intersections of the parabola with the $x$-axis. Connecting $OC$, $AB$,\\
as shown in the figure,\\
the shaded area equals the area of $\triangle ABCO$, with $S=2\times 3=\boxed{6}$.

First read from the image that the shaded region lies between the x-axis and the horizontal line y = -3, with two congruent upward-opening parabolas whose vertices lie on y = -3; the shifted parabola has its vertex on the y-axis and the original one has its vertex to the right. From the text/equation, complete the square: y = x^2 - 4x + 1 = (x - 2)^2 - 3, so the original vertex is C(2, -3). After shifting left to put the vertex on the y-axis, the new vertex is B(0, -3). Thus the two vertices are horizontally 2 units apart and vertically 3 units below the x-axis. Complete the rectangle with corners O(0,0), A(2,0), C(2,-3), B(0,-3). The figure indicates that the curvilinear shaded shape differs from this rectangle only by congruent parabolic pieces cut from one side and added to the other, because the two parabolas are horizontal translates of each other. Therefore the shaded area equals the rectangle area: width 2 times height 3, giving S = 6.

From the image, observe that the shaded region is swept between the horizontal levels y = -3 and y = 0, bounded laterally by corresponding branches of two identical parabolas shifted horizontally. From the text, rewrite the original parabola as y = (x - 2)^2 - 3, so its vertex is at (2,-3); after shifting left, the other parabola is y = x^2 - 3 with vertex at (0,-3). For any horizontal level between y = -3 and y = 0, the relevant shaded cross-sections shown in the figure have total horizontal length equal to the fixed horizontal separation between corresponding translated parabolic branches, namely 2. As shown in the figure, connecting \(OC\) and \(AB\), the shaded area equals the area of \(\triangle ABCO\), so \(S=2\times 3=\boxed{6}\).
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: After shifting the parabola \(y=x^{2}-4x+1\) to the left so that its vertex falls on the y-axis, as shown in the figure, what is the area \(S\) of the shape formed by the two parabolas, the line \(y=-3\), and the x-axis (the shaded area in the figure)?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The parabola \(y=x^{2}-4x+1=(x-2)^{2}-3\) has vertex \(C(2,-3)\). After shifting left so the vertex lies on the y-axis, the new vertex is \(B(0,-3)\). Let \(A\) be one intersection of the parabola with the x-axis. As shown in the figure, connecting \(OC\) and \(AB\), the shaded area equals the area of \(\triangle ABCO\), so \(S=2\times 3=\boxed{6}\).
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure there are two parabolas opening upward, one with its vertex on the y-axis and the other with its vertex to the right of it; their vertices are both on the horizontal straight line y=-3. The x-axis is also drawn in the figure, as well as the lower straight line y=-3. The shaded part is exactly the region enclosed by the two parabolas, the x-axis, and y=-3.

Then reason: The original parabola y=x^2-4x+1 can be completed to the square as y=(x-2)^2-3, so its vertex is C(2,-3). Translate it to the left so that the vertex falls on the y-axis, obtaining the new vertex B(0,-3). From the figure, the two parabolas are only in a horizontal translation relationship, therefore the shaded region can, by a “compensation” idea, be regarded as having the same area as rectangle OACB: the width of the rectangle is 2, and the height is 3. Thus the area
S=2×3=6.

Therefore the shaded area is 6.
